summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen, angered by John L. Sullivan's remarks about Zachritz, confronted Sullivan behind the footlights of the People's Theater before friends hustled the two apart.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Friday, May 9, 1884, page 4. article.json has no focus field.

facts.fact: Allen confronted John L. Sullivan behind the footlights of the People's Theater in St. Louis over Sullivan's remarks about Zachritz; friends separated them before a row
Allen told Sullivan he could beat any man in Sullivan's gang except Sullivan
facts.quote: Of course you can come here and make your bluffs. We can't stop that, but I can do up any man in your gang except Sullivan, and I'm just as good a man as Sullivan with my clothes on.
